page: Microsoft Azure E96-24s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine deployed via Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, configured with 24 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped across 12 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled at 4.2 GHz. The CPU subsystem is equipped with a large 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and hardware support for advanced vector and matrix instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX. The instance features a constrained CPU core count paired with a full-chassis memory footprint of 768.0 GB of RAM, resulting in a high allocation of 32.0 GB of memory per vCPU. The server does not bundle local disk storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark measurements reflect high memory throughput and solid single-core compute performance. In Geekbench testing, the instance logged a single-core score of 2,142.0 (placing in the top 25%), while its multi-core score registered at 15,298.0. Uncached large-block memory write bandwidth was strong at 116.85 GB/sec, complemented by an uncached read throughput of 187.67 GB/sec. Across specialized compute benchmarks, the system achieved top-quartile results in Geekbench text processing (2,674.0), image processing (15,048.0), and small model LLM text generation at 294.92 tokens/sec. General multi-core tests, such as stress-ng (23,968.2) and PassMark CPU (37,633.32), ranked within the average tier.

The constrained vCPU architecture provides substantial cost efficiency for software deployments that are priced per core or per socket while demanding massive working memory. By provisioning 768.0 GB of RAM against only 24 vCPUs, operations avoid paying software license fees for unused compute capacity. Because no local storage is provided, persistent IOPS and disk storage require external network-attached volumes. This instance is best suited for memory-intensive workloads including large in-memory databases, SAP HANA, Redis caching clusters, analytics platforms, and enterprise ERP systems.

It provides 24 dedicated vCPUs (12 physical cores with hyperthreading) and an expansive 768.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a high 32.0 GB per vCPU ratio alongside 260 MB of L3 cache. The instance excludes local disk storage and GPU hardware, depending entirely on remote storage. In benchmark evaluations, the E96-24s_v6 delivers strong single-core performance with a Geekbench single-core score of 2,142.0, robust uncached memory write bandwidth of 116.85 GB/sec, and efficient small-model text generation. With core-constrained compute paired with large memory reserves, this server is well suited for memory-bound relational databases, large-scale Redis caching, and enterprise applications sensitive to per-core software licensing costs.
